zh.title: 史瓦帝尼政府A340專機由桃園轉場高雄　轉場目的尚待官方說明
zh.summary: 航跡顯示，史瓦帝尼政府A340專機3DC-SDF今日由桃園機場轉場高雄機場，實際轉場目的尚未獲官方確認。該機前身為中華航空B-18802，此次搭載史國國王及訪團來臺參加國慶並進行國是訪問。
body: 公開航跡顯示，史瓦帝尼王國政府一架Airbus A340-313X專機於今（14）日中午自桃園國際機場（TPE）起飛，轉場前往高雄國際機場（KHH）。航班追蹤資料列出該機於臺北時間下午12時05分起飛，原預計下午1時24分抵達高雄。目前尚未取得官方對此次轉場目的的說明，無法僅憑航跡確認是否涉及航機保養或其他安排。
這架專機此次來臺，是搭載史瓦帝尼國王恩史瓦帝三世、祖瑪王妃及隨行訪團參加我國國慶慶典並進行國是訪問。外交部資料顯示，訪團於10月9日至17日停留臺灣，此行是恩史瓦帝三世自1986年即位以來第20次率團訪臺；這項訪團行程資訊並未說明專機此次轉場高雄的具體用途。
執飛航機註冊編號為3DC-SDF，製造序號406，目前由史瓦帝尼政府使用，主要執行王室及政府外訪任務。該機型採用4具CFM International CFM56-5C4發動機，具備執行長程航線的能力。
3DC-SDF與臺灣航空業淵源深厚，前身為中華航空B-18802，於2001年交付華航，2015年退出營運並飛往美國封存。史瓦帝尼王國於2016年購入該機，經過約兩年的整修及行政專機改裝後，於2018年正式交付史國政府使用。太報過往報導曾提及該機的技術訓練及維修支援與臺灣航空維修體系保持聯繫，但這項歷史背景不足以證實此次轉場高雄是為了保養。
A340-300是空中巴士研製的四發動機廣體客機，過去曾廣泛用於長程國際航線。隨著航空公司逐步改用油耗較低的雙發動機廣體客機，目前仍在全球執行任務的A340-300數量已明顯減少。3DC-SDF此次由桃園轉場高雄，也使這架具有華航歷史的史瓦帝尼政府專機再度受到臺灣航空攝影愛好者關注。
另據悉，該機將在高雄停留至至少10月17日，配合國王結束訪臺行程。外交部公布的訪團行程至17日止，但航機停留期間、實際離場日期、起飛時間及是否直接自高雄離臺，目前尚未獲官方公開確認。未能看到或拍攝此次降落的航迷與民眾，仍可能有機會在該機離場時拍攝起飛；實際飛航安排應以後續官方資訊及航班動態為準。

en.title: Eswatini Government A340 Repositions From Taoyuan to Kaohsiung; Purpose Awaiting Official Confirmation
en.summary: Flight tracking shows Eswatini government A340 3DC-SDF, formerly China Airlines B-18802, repositioning from Taoyuan Airport to Kaohsiung Airport today. The purpose remains unconfirmed by officials. The aircraft brought the royal delegation to Taiwan for National Day celebrations and a state visit.
body: Public flight tracking shows an Eswatini government Airbus A340-313X departing Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport (TPE) around midday today, October 14, to reposition to Kaohsiung International Airport (KHH). Tracking data recorded departure at 12:05 Taipei time and initially estimated arrival in Kaohsiung at 13:24. No official explanation of the purpose of this repositioning has been obtained, and the flight path alone cannot establish whether it involves aircraft maintenance or other arrangements.

The aircraft came to Taiwan carrying King Mswati III of Eswatini, Inkhosikati Make Zuma and their accompanying delegation for National Day celebrations and a state visit. Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the delegation's visit runs from October 9 to 17. This is the king's 20th visit to Taiwan since his accession in 1986. The delegation's itinerary does not specify the purpose of the aircraft's repositioning to Kaohsiung.

The aircraft is registered 3DC-SDF and carries manufacturer serial number 406. It is used by the Eswatini government primarily for royal and government overseas visits. The aircraft has four CFM International CFM56-5C4 engines and is capable of long-haul operations.

3DC-SDF has longstanding ties to Taiwan's aviation industry. It previously operated as China Airlines B-18802, was delivered to the airline in 2001, and left service in 2015 before being flown to the United States for storage. Eswatini purchased the aircraft in 2016. Following approximately two years of refurbishment and conversion for government transport, it was delivered to the country's government in 2018. A previous TaiSounds report described links between the aircraft's technical training and maintenance support and Taiwan's aircraft maintenance sector. That historical background does not establish that this repositioning to Kaohsiung is for maintenance.

The Airbus A340-300 is a four-engine widebody aircraft that was once widely used on long-haul international services. As airlines have increasingly adopted more fuel-efficient twin-engine widebodies, the number of A340-300s still operating worldwide has declined markedly. The repositioning of 3DC-SDF from Taoyuan to Kaohsiung has again drawn the attention of aviation photographers in Taiwan to this former China Airlines aircraft.

The aircraft is reportedly expected to remain in Kaohsiung until at least October 17 in connection with the conclusion of the king's Taiwan visit. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the delegation's visit as ending on October 17, but the aircraft's length of stay, actual departure date and time, and whether it will leave Taiwan directly from Kaohsiung have not been publicly confirmed by officials. Aviation enthusiasts and members of the public who missed its arrival may still have an opportunity to photograph its departure. Actual flight arrangements remain subject to subsequent official information and flight updates.
